source.place: Proof step 1: injective-target derived homology comparison

proof.text: For a cochain complex P and a morphism g from its degree-zero homology to that of I[0], compose g with HomologicalComplex.singleObjHomologySelfIso to obtain a morphism to I. Extend this along the monomorphism P.homologyι 0 using Injective.factorThru. Precompose the extension with P.pOpcycles 0 and use HomologicalComplex.d_pOpcycles to construct a chain map with HomologicalComplex.mkHomToSingle. Cancel the target homology isomorphism and the epimorphism P.homologyπ 0. Naturality of homologyπ, cyclesMap_i, homology_π_ι, and Injective.comp_factorThru prove that the constructed chain map induces exactly g. This is the fully proved private helper homology_to_single_surjective; it uses only Mathlib.

Choose a complex P and an isomorphism e: Q(P) ≅ K using the essential surjectivity of DerivedCategory.Q. Transport the prescribed derived homology map along e and the natural isomorphism DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors, apply the preceding chain-level construction, and take e.inv followed by Q.map of the resulting chain map. Naturality of homologyFunctorFactors and the two inverse-isomorphism identities give the required equality on homology. No K-injective replacement, representation of arbitrary derived morphisms by chain maps, or additional Sheaf theorem is used.

title: Surjectivity of the degree-zero homology map from morphisms into an injective single object.
statement: For an abelian category A with a chosen derived category, K in D(A), and injective I in A, the degree-zero homology map from morphisms K to I[0] to morphisms between degree-zero homology objects is surjective.

lean.statement:
theorem derived_homology_injective_surjective
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    (K : DerivedCategory A) (I : A) [Injective I] :
    Function.Surjective
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A 0).map :
        (K ⟶ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj I) →
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A 0).obj K ⟶
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A 0).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj I)))
